key_insight: Composition anisotropy in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics creates an unexpectedly huge bulk photovoltaic field along the non-polar vertical direction, far exceeding the polar in-plane response.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-gain, voltage-readout photodetectors and other photoferroelectric devices that exploit directional photovoltage rather than only conventional polar-axis transport.
method: Studied 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics with strong inorganic/organic compositional anisotropy.
Analyzed bulk photovoltaic effect behavior and shift-current-driven photovoltage along polar and non-polar directions.
Developed formulas describing laser-intensity and thickness-dependent photovoltage scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the vertical nonpolar EBPE is up to two orders of magnitude larger than the polar in-plane direction and is the highest among reported 2D HPFs.
watch_item: Device performance may depend strongly on composition, anisotropy, and thickness, so scaling this effect to practical architectures will require careful control of material uniformity and orientation.
paper_title: Composition Anisotropy Drives Large Bulk Photovoltaic Fields Along the Non-polar Vertical Direction in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectrics
